source_install_reuse.rule: Install BPM inside Ubuntu 26.04 WSL from the exact documented Linux userspace procedure. The runner verifies the installed checkout and must not replace package, Python, Git, migration, or documentation commands with a Windows-native path.
source_install_reuse.wsl_runtime_adapter: Bind the foreground development runtime to 0.0.0.0 only for bounded Windows-host localhost and browser validation; this does not change the documented Linux installation commands or authorize external exposure.

checks.pass_rule: The observed caption identifies the requested Windows 10 or Windows 11 target.
The requested distribution exists and reports WSL generation 2; missing version output blocks validation.
ID=ubuntu and VERSION_ID=26.04 are observed inside the requested WSL distribution.
The mode is recorded as enabled/running, enabled/degraded, or not enabled; BPM remains a foreground source process and no service claim is inferred.
The checkout resolves under /home and not through a Windows-mounted or host-shared filesystem.
The checkout matches the approved ref and the accepted Linux userspace post-install assertions pass.
The first and post-restart runtime cycles answer from both WSL loopback and Windows localhost.
Windows Edge loads the BPM Library route and returns an HTML document in both runtime cycles.
The foreground BPM process stops and both sides reject the health probe.
The requested distribution terminates and restarts without preserving the old BPM process, then the second complete runtime cycle passes.
Every command, output, exit code, observable result, failure, and artifact hash is retained without credentials.

workflow.preflight_only: Records host, WSL, distribution, systemd, filesystem, source-ref, Python, and browser executable feasibility without starting BPM or terminating WSL.
full_validation: Run the actual-host and installed-source preflight.
Run migration and all six-locale documentation validation/build/dev-install assertions.
Start BPM inside WSL with the bounded WSL runtime adapter.
Verify WSL probes, Windows localhost probes, and Windows Edge access.
Stop BPM and prove connection refusal from WSL and Windows.
Terminate and restart only the named WSL distribution.
Recheck identity and prove the old BPM process is absent.
Repeat start, WSL/Windows probes, Windows Edge access, and clean stop.
Write a pass or blocked summary and SHA-256 inventory.
workflow.success_claim: Runner execution may close only the supplied Windows target. Preparing or statically testing the runner closes no Windows 10/11 or WSL evidence gap.

sanitization: Do not pass or record passwords, tokens, private keys, cookies, browser profiles, customer data, or production database contents.
Record environment variable names but not secret values.
Use only a fresh local SQLite database created by the documented source-install procedure.
Retain raw command output only inside the run evidence directory.
evidence.handoff: M11-11 or M11-12 commits a sanitized manifest and hashes under documentation/evidence/live-source-install/0.9.1 while raw Windows-host transcripts remain in the recorded local evidence root.

runner_may: read Windows and WSL version/build information
run commands only in the explicitly named WSL distribution
start and stop the BPM foreground development process
terminate and restart only the explicitly named WSL distribution
launch headless Windows Edge against localhost
runner_must_not: install, update, unregister, export, import, or remove WSL or any distribution
run Docker or treat a Linux container as WSL evidence
change Windows Firewall, portproxy, Hyper-V, virtualization, registry, service, scheduled-task, IIS, proxy, TLS, DNS, or network settings
add a Windows service or native installer
delete a checkout, database, distribution, Docker resource, or unrelated evidence
claim production readiness or native Windows support
